sections:
White Plains is the Westchester County seat and is served by Con Edison. Its mix of single-family homes and condos means both the single-family and apartment amounts below can apply, depending on your building.

White Plains has many 1950s–80s single-family homes with ducts already in place for central air. When the ducts are in good shape, a ducted cold-climate heat pump can replace the furnace and the AC in one step.

The city also has lots of condos and co-ops downtown, where the apartment amounts apply and board approval is often needed for outdoor equipment.

Westchester County has its own programs from time to time, so ask your contractor whether a county incentive is open when you apply, but don’t count on one until it is confirmed in writing.

Clean Heat is the Con Edison rebate, so never add the two together. Clean Heat is capped at 70% of cost (85% in a DAC). There is no separate federal HEAR cheque: New York delivers it through EmPower+. The federal 25C/25D tax credits ended December 31, 2025.

Income-qualified? EmPower+ can cover far more than the utility rebate. Check the state DAC map too: it can raise your amount.

Con Edison has no rebate for buying a home charger. Its SmartCharge New York program pays about $400 a year on average for charging off-peak. PowerReady stopped taking new Level 2 applications on April 22, 2026.
claim_heading: What to do next in White Plains
claim_steps: Have your ducts checked for leaks and size before choosing a ducted system.
Condo owners: ask your board about rules for outdoor units first.
Get 2–3 quotes and ask each contractor to show the rebate tier on the quote.
faq: How much is the heat pump rebate in White Plains?

NYS Clean Heat (run by Con Edison) pays up to $11,000 (Disadvantaged Community, Weatherized Tier, old system removed) for a whole-home heat pump in White Plains, depending on home size, whether you remove the old system, and DAC status.
Can I reuse my ducts in White Plains?
Often, yes. Many homes here have central air ducts. A contractor should test them for leaks and size; leaky or undersized ducts should be fixed or the system will not keep up in winter.
Is the federal tax credit still available for heat pumps?
No. The federal 25C and 25D credits ended for anything installed after December 31, 2025.

Lower-income owners and renters of 1-4 family homes. Low-income households can get free upgrades up to $12,000 upstate or $14,000 downstate; moderate-income households get 50% covered up to $6,000 upstate or $7,000 downstate.
